GEOL 101.description: Origin and nature of the earth with emphasis on internal processes and phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain building; surface processes, including landform evolution. Three lectures and three laboratory hours each week.
GEOL 101.subject: GEOL
GEOL 101.title: Introduction to the Earth

GEOL 102.description: Basic overview of fossils, including dinosaurs, and their importance for understanding earth history and the evolution of life. Three lectures and three laboratory hours each week.
GEOL 102.subject: GEOL
GEOL 102.title: Fossils and the Evolution of Life on Earth

GEOL 103.description: Analysis of basic energy cycles of the earth. Interaction of human activity with earth processes to affect the environment. Three lectures and three laboratory hours each week. Field trips required.
GEOL 103.subject: GEOL
GEOL 103.title: Environment of the Earth

GEOL 110.description: The growth of geological concepts, scientific and non-scientific. The impact of geological factors on human affairs. The role of time and evolution (biological and physical). Restricted to non-science majors.
GEOL 110.subject: GEOL
GEOL 110.title: Cultural Geology

GEOL 170.description: Introduction to the origin of water and water properties, water in the universe, water in the solar system, water on Earth and its geological history.
GEOL 170.subject: GEOL
GEOL 170.title: The Water Planet

GEOL 201.description: An introduction to study of the earth through observation of ancient and modern earth systems in a field setting. Field trips required.
GEOL 201.subject: GEOL
GEOL 201.title: Observing the Earth

GEOL 205.description: Mineral, energy, and water resources with emphasis on geological processes governing their distribution. Intended for non-science majors. Three lecture hours each week with occasional field trips.
GEOL 205.subject: GEOL
GEOL 205.title: Earth Resources

GEOL 215.description: Coastal zones of South Carolina and neighboring states, including geologic history, geomorphology, stratigraphy, hydrogeology, shoreline processes, environmental issues, and effects of man. Not available for geological science or marine science major credit. Three lecture hours each week plus optional field trips.
GEOL 215.subject: GEOL
GEOL 215.title: Coastal Environments of the Southeastern U.S.

GEOL 215L.description: Exercises examining coastal ecology, geomorphology, hydrogeology, shoreline processes, environmental issues, and human impact. Not available for marine science major credit. Two laboratory hours per week. Scheduled field trips required.
GEOL 215L.subject: GEOL
GEOL 215L.title: Coastal Environments of the Southeastern U.S. (Laboratory)

GEOL 230.description: Examination of the geologic setting and scientific significance of selected National Parks. Three lecture hours.
GEOL 230.subject: GEOL
GEOL 230.title: Geology of the National Parks

GEOL 302.description: Chemical and physical processes of mineral formation in earth systems including an overview of igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rock-forming processes. Includes laboratory. Field trips required.
GEOL 302.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101, GEOL 103, or GEOL 201; CHEM 111 recommended.
GEOL 302.subject: GEOL
GEOL 302.title: Rocks and Minerals

GEOL 305.description: Survey of earth history, the evolution of continents and oceans, the history of life, and geological dating methods. Includes laboratory and recitation. Required field trips. Taught alternate years.
GEOL 305.subject: GEOL
GEOL 305.title: Earth Systems through Time

GEOL 310.description: Environmental considerations of the hydrologic cycle. Occurrence and movement of surface water and groundwater as they relate to water budgets, water supply, and ecosystems. Geochemistry of natural waters, water quality, and pollution.
GEOL 310.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or higher in MATH 122 or MATH 141; C or higher in GEOL 101, GEOL 103, GEOL 201, GEOG 104, GEOG 201, ENVR 101, ENVR 201, ECIV 101 or MSCI 101.
GEOL 310.subject: GEOL
GEOL 310.title: Surface and Subsurface Hydrology

GEOL 315.description: Overview of groundwater, surface water hydrology, sediment transport, river systems, and coastal processes. Includes laboratory and recitation. Required field trips.
GEOL 315.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
GEOL 315.subject: GEOL
GEOL 315.title: Surface and Near Surface Processes

GEOL 318.description: Directed field studies of extraordinary geological locations in North America. Requires a seven- to nine-day field trip during spring break.
GEOL 318.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101, GEOL 103, or GEOL 201 and consent of instructor.
GEOL 318.subject: GEOL
GEOL 318.title: Field Studies in Geology

GEOL 325.description: Overview of sedimentary basins, sediment transport, sedimentation, depositional environments, stratigraphy, seismic stratigraphy, eustacy, and sedimentary petrology. Includes laboratory and recitation. Required field trips.
GEOL 325.subject: GEOL
GEOL 325.title: Stratigraphy and Sedimentary Basins

GEOL 335.description: The science of global change, its relation to the hydrosphere, atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere. Global system science, biogeochemical cycles, paleoclimatology, glaciation, and eustacy.
GEOL 335.subject: GEOL
GEOL 335.title: Processes of Global Environmental Change

GEOL 345.description: Origin and significance of igneous and metamorphic rocks, and relation to tectonic processes. Mineralogy, geochemistry, volcanism, plate tectonics, isostasy, heat flow. Includes laboratory and recitation. Required field trips.
GEOL 345.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 302; D or better in MATH 122 or MATH 141.
GEOL 345.subject: GEOL
GEOL 345.title: Igneous and Metamorphic Processes

GEOL 355.description: Geologic structures and deformation of Earth materials. Stress and strain, deformation mechanisms, P-T-t paths, geologic maps, and structural regimes in plate tectonics. Includes laboratory and recitation. Required field trips.
GEOL 355.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 302; D or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
GEOL 355.subject: GEOL
GEOL 355.title: Structural Geology and Tectonics

GEOL 360.description: Exploration of post-graduation opportunities in academia and industry. Interactive discussion of topics including helping skills, active listening, oral communication, goal setting, interviewing, and building a strong professional portfolio.
GEOL 360.subject: GEOL
GEOL 360.title: SEOE Peer Mentorship, Leadership, Professional Development

GEOL 365.description: Computational analysis of earth, marine, and environmental datasets applying time series analysis, regression, filtering, and statistical analysis.
GEOL 365.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 106 or higher; C or better in MATH 122 or higher.
GEOL 365.subject: GEOL
GEOL 365.title: Data Science in Earth, Ocean and Environmental Science

GEOL 371.description: Introduction to terrestrial and tidal river morphology and processes, with case studies of South Carolina. Field trips required.
GEOL 371.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101, GEOL 103, or GEOL 201.
GEOL 371.subject: GEOL
GEOL 371.title: A View of the River

GEOL 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
GEOL 399.subject: GEOL
GEOL 399.title: Independent Study

GEOL 495.description: Supervised internship experience in a professional environment within the field of geology and/or related geological sciences. Undergraduate internship contract required with approval of instructor, advisor, and department head before registration.
GEOL 495.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101, GEOL 103 or GEOL 201; C or better in one other GEOL course at or above the 300 level.
GEOL 495.subject: GEOL
GEOL 495.title: Internship in the Geological Science

GEOL 498.description: Student research on problems of regional and fundamental significance, supervised by a faculty member of the student’s choice. Emphasis is on the development of critical thinking and lucid scientific report writing.
GEOL 498.subject: GEOL
GEOL 498.title: Undergraduate Research

GEOL 499.description: Student research on problems of regional and fundamental significance, supervised by a faculty member of the student’s choice. Emphasis is on the development of critical thinking and lucid scientific report writing.
GEOL 499.subject: GEOL
GEOL 499.title: Undergraduate Research

GEOL 500.description: Geological field techniques including the use of field instruments and the preparation of geologic maps. Written and oral reports required.
GEOL 500.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 325 and GEOL 355.
GEOL 500.subject: GEOL
GEOL 500.title: Field Geology

GEOL 500L.description: Introduction to geological field techniques and review of core field geology concepts in preparation for an extended field experience.
GEOL 500L.subject: GEOL
GEOL 500L.title: Introduction to Field Geology

GEOL 501.description: The process of earth denudation with emphasis on chemistry of weathering, stream and erosion hydraulics, quantitative analysis of land form evolution.
GEOL 501.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101.
GEOL 501.subject: GEOL
GEOL 501.title: Principles of Geomorphology

GEOL 502.description: Geological and physical controls on the morphology, development, and stability of coastlines. Analysis of waves and erosional processes, and coastal zone morphodynamics. Several required field trips.
GEOL 502.subject: GEOL
GEOL 502.title: Principles of Coastal Geomorphology

GEOL 503.description: Sedimentologic, biostratigraphic, and tectonic history of North America, approached from paleogeographic considerations with emphasis on the Atlantic Coastal Plain and Continental Margin. Three hours lecture and three hours recitation per week. Required field trips.
GEOL 503.subject: GEOL
GEOL 503.title: Regional Stratigraphy and Biostratigraphy of North America

GEOL 504.description: This course will discuss the urgent need for deploying solar radiation and carbon dioxide removal approaches at scale, including potential benefits and risks of these options. It will also discuss regulatory and governance considerations at both the national and international level and strategizes to incentivize large-scale adoption of these approaches.
GEOL 504.subject: GEOL
GEOL 504.title: Climate Geoengineering

GEOL 511.description: Systematic, ecologic, biogeographic, and evolutionary aspects of paleontology; lectures, practical exercises, field trips.
GEOL 511.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 305.
GEOL 511.subject: GEOL
GEOL 511.title: Advanced Paleontology

GEOL 515.description: Marine microfossils; distribution, ecology, paleoecology, and biostratigraphy; use of microfossils in marine sediments to study oceanographic history. Three lectures and two laboratory hours per week.
GEOL 515.subject: GEOL
GEOL 515.title: Marine Micropaleontology

GEOL 516.description: Modern concepts of sediment composition, sedimentary facies, depositional environments, and stratigraphy. Includes laboratory.
GEOL 516.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 325.
GEOL 516.subject: GEOL
GEOL 516.title: Sedimentology

GEOL 518.description: Surface to subsurface stratigraphic interpretation and techniques; litho- and biostratigraphy; geophysical log interpretation and subsurface presentation.
GEOL 518.subject: GEOL
GEOL 518.title: Surface to Subsurface Stratigraphy

GEOL 520.description: Dating techniques for Pleistocene deposits, sediments, archaeological materials, igneous and metamorphic rocks.
GEOL 520.subject: GEOL
GEOL 520.title: Isotope Geology and Geochronology

GEOL 521.description: Investigation of low temperature chemical reactions controlling the geochemistry of the earth’s surface. Emphasis on CO2, carbonates, oxidation-reduction, thermodynamics, isotopes, biogeochemistry.
GEOL 521.subject: GEOL
GEOL 521.title: Introduction to Geochemistry

GEOL 524.description: Introduction to radioactivity and the use of radionuclides to study environmental processes, including age-dating and biogeochemical cycling in aquatic systems.
GEOL 524.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CHEM 111, CHEM 112 and MATH 141.
GEOL 524.subject: GEOL
GEOL 524.title: Environmental Radioisotope Geochemistry

GEOL 526.description: Petrography and petrogenesis of igneous rocks; evolution of contrasting petrotectonic terranes. Three lectures and three laboratory hours per week.
GEOL 526.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 302.
GEOL 526.subject: GEOL
GEOL 526.title: Igneous Petrology

GEOL 527.description: Petrography and petrogenesis of metamorphic rocks in orogenic belts. Three lectures and three laboratory hours per week.
GEOL 527.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 302.
GEOL 527.subject: GEOL
GEOL 527.title: Metamorphic Petrology

GEOL 531.description: Geological and geophysical evidence for plate tectonics, detailed development of the plate tectonics model, and present areas of research, including measurements of plate motion using satellite geodesy.
GEOL 531.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in two GEOL courses numbered 300 or above, or consent of instructor.
GEOL 531.subject: GEOL
GEOL 531.title: Plate Tectonics

GEOL 537.description: Application of two or more geophysical field methods to a current geological problem. Independent study contract required.
GEOL 537.subject: GEOL
GEOL 537.title: Field Methods in Geophysics

GEOL 540.description: Origin, internal structure and internal processes of the earth, including plate tectonics, earthquakes, volcanoes, and mountain building. Required field trips, two lectures, and three lab hours per week. Cannot be used in MS or PhD programs in geology.
GEOL 540.subject: GEOL
GEOL 540.title: Earth Science for Teachers I

GEOL 541.description: Surface processes acting on the earth; introduction to weather and climate, weathering, erosion, and sedimentary processes; land form evolution; ocean currents and tides, near-shore geologic processes. Required field trips, two lecture, and three lab hours per week. Cannot be used in MS or PhD programs in geology.
GEOL 541.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in EDSE 548 or C or better in GEOL 540.
GEOL 541.subject: GEOL
GEOL 541.title: Earth Science for Teachers II

GEOL 542.description: Introduction to methods used in discipline-based education research and their application to research questions in the geosciences.
GEOL 542.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in least one course in GEOL, ENVR, MSCI or GEOG.
GEOL 542.subject: GEOL
GEOL 542.title: Methods in Geoscience Education Research

GEOL 545.description: A comprehensive study of the origin and development of the major structural features of the ocean basins and the continental margins. Discussion of the techniques used in obtaining geologic data and the interpretation of sedimentary processes, vulcanism, and the stratigraphy of the ocean basins.
GEOL 545.subject: GEOL
GEOL 545.title: Geological Oceanography

GEOL 546.description: Introduction to the nature and structure of the ocean floor as revealed by geophysical techniques. Two hours lecture and three hours laboratory.
GEOL 546.subject: GEOL
GEOL 546.title: Marine Geophysics

GEOL 548.description: Practical geophysical techniques for exploring the shallow subsurface. Seismic, resistivity, well log, gravity, magnetic method. Includes lectures and field exercises to collect and analyze data.
GEOL 548.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 141; D or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
GEOL 548.subject: GEOL
GEOL 548.title: Environmental Geophysics

GEOL 550.description: Problems of sequence stratigraphy resolved with graphic computer simulations. Sedimentary fill of basins by carbonates and/or clastics tracked as a function of rate of sediment accumulation, tectonic behavior, and sea level. Includes laboratory.
GEOL 550.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 325.
GEOL 550.subject: GEOL
GEOL 550.title: Sedimentary Simulations and Sequence Stratigraphy

GEOL 553.description: Marine sedimentary environments; physical/biological factors which control the formation and distribution of modern marine sediments.
GEOL 553.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 516.
GEOL 553.subject: GEOL
GEOL 553.title: Marine Sediments

GEOL 554.description: Theory of seismic wave propagation. Seismic reflection data acquisition, processing, and interpretation.
GEOL 554.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 141; D or better in PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
GEOL 554.subject: GEOL
GEOL 554.title: Applied Seismology

GEOL 555.description: Basic elements of seismology. Mathematical development of seismic wave equations; measurement, description, and interpretation of seismic data.
GEOL 555.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 241.
GEOL 555.subject: GEOL
GEOL 555.title: Elementary Seismology

GEOL 556.description: The interpretation of geologic structure using seismic sections. Recognition of apparent structure caused by velocity anomalies, multiples, and complex reflector geometry. Application to hydrocarbon exploration.
GEOL 556.subject: GEOL
GEOL 556.title: Seismic Reflection Interpretation

GEOL 557.description: Physical and geological processes controlling the formation and evolution of beach, barrier, and nearshore environments, including discussion of coastal management issues.
GEOL 557.subject: GEOL
GEOL 557.title: Coastal Processes

GEOL 560.description: An approach to problems of resource management by lecture and seminar using case studies in mineral, energy, hydrogeological, and environmental science.
GEOL 560.subject: GEOL
GEOL 560.title: Earth Resource Management

GEOL 561.description: An introduction to field methods in sedimentology, structural geology, hydrogeology and geophysics with special reference to geological hazards and environmental problems.
GEOL 561.subject: GEOL
GEOL 561.title: Environmental Field Geology

GEOL 567.description: Climatic changes of the past and their impact on the physical landscape, with an emphasis on the Quaternary period.
GEOL 567.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in a 200-level course in physical geography or geology or equivalent.
GEOL 567.subject: GEOL
GEOL 567.title: Long-Term Environmental Change

GEOL 568.description: Small-scale processes in the atmospheric boundary layers, including energy budget, radiation, soil heat transfer, humidity, viscous flows, turbulence, momentum and heat exchanges, evaporation, and marine atmospheric boundary layer.
GEOL 568.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in PHYS 201 and MATH 141.
GEOL 568.subject: GEOL
GEOL 568.title: Introduction to Micrometeorology

GEOL 570.description: Environmental considerations of the hydrologic cycle, occurrence and movement of ground water, aquifer analysis, and water well emplacement and construction. Water quality, pollution parameters, and the geochemistry of selected natural systems. The effects of environmental problems, waste disposal, and urban development upon the aqueous geochemical regime.
GEOL 570.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101 and D or better in CHEM 111 or their equivalents.
GEOL 570.subject: GEOL
GEOL 570.title: Environmental Hydrogeology

GEOL 571.description: Saturated and unsaturated water flow through soils, pore pressure development, runoff generation, and watershed response to rainfall. Three lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
GEOL 571.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in PHYS 202 and MATH 142.
GEOL 571.subject: GEOL
GEOL 571.title: Soil Hydrology

GEOL 575.description: Finite difference and finite element methods for solving the diffusion equation and advection-dispersion equation, with applications in hydrogeology, geophysics, geology, and marine science.
GEOL 575.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in MATH 142; MATH 241 is recommended.
GEOL 575.subject: GEOL
GEOL 575.title: Numerical Modeling for Earth Science Applications

GEOL 579.description: The physical mechanism responsible for interaction between the ocean and the atmosphere and the influence of air-sea interaction on atmospheric and oceanic dynamics and thermodynamics on a wide variety of spatial/temporal scales.
GEOL 579.subject: GEOL
GEOL 579.title: Air-Sea Interaction

GEOL 580.description: This course provides knowledge of various techniques used in satellite remote sensing of the oceans. Key skills will be developed in satellite data processing, image analysis, and hands-on research.
GEOL 580.subject: GEOL
GEOL 580.title: Satellite Oceanography

GEOL 581.description: Estuarine kinematics and dynamics; classification of estuaries; estuarine circulation and mixing. Scheduled field trips are required.
GEOL 581.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MSCI 314.
GEOL 581.subject: GEOL
GEOL 581.title: Estuarine Oceanography

GEOL 582.description: Basic principles of fluid statics and dynamics. Conservation of mass, momentum, and energy; viscosity, vorticity, and boundary layers with examples from the marine environment. Applications to and analysis of ocean currents and waves.
GEOL 582.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in MATH 241 and C or better in either PHYS 201 or PHYS 211.
GEOL 582.subject: GEOL
GEOL 582.title: Marine Hydrodynamics

GEOL 583.description: Geological and geochemical processes in salt marshes. Methods of geological research in marshes including instrumental techniques, sampling design, and data analysis. Two lectures per week plus four weekends of project oriented fieldwork and/or equivalent lab work. Scheduled field trips are required.
GEOL 583.subject: GEOL
GEOL 583.title: Geology and Geochemistry of Salt Marshes

GEOL 599.description: Current developments in geological science selected to meet faculty and student interests. Course content varies and will be announced by title in schedule of courses.
GEOL 599.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in GEOL 101, GEOL 103 or GEOL 201 or graduate student standing in the School of the Earth, Ocean and Environment (SEOE).
GEOL 599.subject: GEOL
GEOL 599.title: Topics in Geological Science

GEOL 600.description: Advanced research topics in geology and geophysics; critical reading of literature, technical presentations, and written reports. Senior standing.
GEOL 600.subject: GEOL
GEOL 600.title: Senior Seminar in Geology and Geophysics

GEOL 650.description: SEM, ESEM, TEM, and EMPA, WDS quantitative analysis, EDS semi-quantitative analysis, EBSD, methods of sample preparation, and applications in varieties of disciplines. Two lecture and three laboratory hours per week.
GEOL 650.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: D or better in CHEM 111 or equivalent.
GEOL 650.subject: GEOL
GEOL 650.title: Electron Microscopy and Microanalysis

GEOL 699.description: Senior capstone experience, research on a problem on fundamental significance, supervised by faculty member; must include field study component, written final project report, and oral presentation at departmental seminar.
GEOL 699.subject: GEOL
GEOL 699.title: Senior Thesis

GEOL 700.description: Survey of the surficial, coastal, and bedrock geology of South Carolina, its regional physiographic and tectonic setting, and the natural resources of the state.
GEOL 700.subject: GEOL
GEOL 700.title: Geology of South Carolina

GEOL 702.description: The hydrologic cycle in geologic settings of this region, and the effects of urbanization and industrialization on groundwater, rivers, and coasts. The vulnerability of urban and industrial systems to natural geologic processes. Two lecture and three laboratory hours per week. Not available for graduate credit for students in M.S. or Ph.D. programs in geological sciences.
GEOL 702.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: introductory course in any of the earth sciences.
GEOL 702.subject: GEOL
GEOL 702.title: Environmental Earth Science for Teachers

GEOL 703.description: Two weekend field courses dealing with Pleistocene and Holocene coastal geology, plate tectonics, sea-level change, global circulation patterns, shoreline change since 1850, and nearshore processes.
GEOL 703.subject: GEOL
GEOL 703.title: Field Studies in Pleistocene and Holocene Geology for Teachers

GEOL 704.description: Two weekend field courses dealing with barrier island and associated marsh environments, marsh productivity, the dune-beach-bar system, shoreline stabilization, and nearshore processes on natural and armored shorelines.
GEOL 704.subject: GEOL
GEOL 704.title: Field Studies for Teachers in Natural and Altered Barrier Island Systems

GEOL 711.description: An overview of Earth’s climate history during Cenozoic. Emphasis will be placed on Pleistocene glacial-interglacial climate variability and understanding the proxies used to reconstruct past climate changes.
GEOL 711.subject: GEOL
GEOL 711.title: Paleoclimatology

GEOL 715.description: Introduction to the analysis of stable isotopes of hydrogen, oxygen, carbon, nitrogen, and sulfur using mass spectrometry. Emphasis will be on the use of these isotopes in geological problems.
GEOL 715.subject: GEOL
GEOL 715.title: Stable Isotope Geochemistry

GEOL 716.description: Relationship of sequence stratigraphy to sea level variations, tectonics and sedimentation. Construction and analyses of paleogeographic maps, regional cross-sections, and chronostratigraphic charts.
GEOL 716.subject: GEOL
GEOL 716.title: Eustasy and Global Variations in Sequence Stratigraphy

GEOL 717.description: Sources, transport, and fate of organic matter in natural environments including soils, riverine, estuarine, coastal and open ocean sediments and waters.
GEOL 717.subject: GEOL
GEOL 717.title: Organic Geochemistry

GEOL 720.description: Principles of atomic structure and chemical variation of minerals.
GEOL 720.subject: GEOL
GEOL 720.title: Crystal Chemistry and Mineral Structure

GEOL 722.description: This course was not found in the supplied content but was listed in the program requirements. If possible, please provide us with the correct information.
GEOL 722.subject: GEOL
GEOL 722.title: Aqueous Geochemistry

GEOL 725.description: Examination of the structure and dynamics of the Earth’s interior combining perspectives from geophysics and geochemistry. Focus on the lithospheric cycle.
GEOL 725.subject: GEOL
GEOL 725.title: Solid Earth Processes

GEOL 726.description: An investigation of igneous processes and their role in crustal genesis and evolution.
GEOL 726.subject: GEOL
GEOL 726.title: Igneous Processes and Crustal Genesis

GEOL 731.description: A study of the deformation of the earth’s crust including mechanics of folding, faulting, jointing, and cleavage formation. Consideration of current theories of orogenesis in relation to geophysical evidence for the structure of the earth’s crust, mantle, and core.
GEOL 731.subject: GEOL
GEOL 731.title: Advanced Structural Geology

GEOL 733.description: Behavior of rocks and minerals up to 10kb, 8000°C. Role of internal pore pressure and time. Interplay of theory and empiricism.
GEOL 733.subject: GEOL
GEOL 733.title: Rock Mechanics

GEOL 735.description: Integrated analysis (from both model and case history approaches) of the regional structural geology of selected classic areas and analysis of the interaction of tectonic and sedimentary processes in the production of the sedimentary sequences of selected geosynclines and basins. Weekend field trips.
GEOL 735.subject: GEOL
GEOL 735.title: Regional Tectonics

GEOL 743.description: Environmental project planning and management. Types and magnitudes of environmental problems; environmental pathways; environmental data acquisition and analysis; protection versus restoration; risk assessment; site assessment.
GEOL 743.subject: GEOL
GEOL 743.title: Decision Making in Environmental Resource Management

GEOL 744.description: An integrative seminar for science managers. Consideration of the technical, managerial, and financial aspects of decision making in geologic enterprises, with emphasis on hydrocarbon exploration.
GEOL 744.subject: GEOL
GEOL 744.title: Decision Making in Energy Resource Management

GEOL 745.description: An introduction to exploring for oil and natural gas; concentration on specific regions with energy resources.
GEOL 745.subject: GEOL
GEOL 745.title: Petroleum Geology

GEOL 750.description: Development of the stratigraphic systems; detailed analysis of the aims, working methods, and relations between litho-, bio-, and chronostratigraphy. Three lecture hours per week with occasional field trips.
GEOL 750.subject: GEOL
GEOL 750.title: Basin Analysis Seminar

GEOL 751.description: Detailed analysis of the processes and products of carbonate sedimentation, diagenesis, and lithification, with special emphasis upon the role of organisms in forming carbonate sediments and sedimentary rocks. Three lecture hours per week with occasional field trips.
GEOL 751.subject: GEOL
GEOL 751.title: Carbonate Petrology

GEOL 752.description: Sandstone properties as a response to geologic processes. Relationships between the porous microstructure of sandstones and fluid transport. Automated petrography using image analysis and pattern recognition procedures.
GEOL 752.subject: GEOL
GEOL 752.title: Sandstone Petrology

GEOL 754.description: Shipboard experience with basic techniques used by geological, physical, chemical, and biological oceanographers.
GEOL 754.subject: GEOL
GEOL 754.title: Oceanographic Techniques

GEOL 755.description: A field and laboratory course designed to acquaint students with basic techniques needed to measure and analyze various biotic and abiotic environmental parameters in estuarine and shallow water habitats. One lecture and six laboratory hours per week.
GEOL 755.subject: GEOL
GEOL 755.title: Environmental Measurements and Analysis

GEOL 758.description: Principles used in processing, smoothing, correlating and contouring geological data and simulating geologic processes.
GEOL 758.subject: GEOL
GEOL 758.title: Analysis of Geological Data

GEOL 764.description: The interpretation of regional stratigraphy and structure using seismic sections. Recognition of stratigraphic sequences, sedimentary facies, and extensional and compressional structures. Application to hydrocarbon exploration.
GEOL 764.subject: GEOL
GEOL 764.title: Seismic Reflection Interpretation

GEOL 765.description: Seismic refraction and reflection methods including sources, instrumentation, data processing, velocity analysis, seismic modeling, and interpretation.
GEOL 765.subject: GEOL
GEOL 765.title: Exploration Seismology

GEOL 766.description: Advanced treatment of elastic wave propagation, ray theory, normal modes, and free oscillations; applications to determine earth structure, modeling of earthquakes.
GEOL 766.subject: GEOL
GEOL 766.title: Advanced Seismology

GEOL 770.description: The evaluation of aquifer characteristics by flow nets, Theis equation and graphic solution technique for water table and artesian conditions. Methodology of pumping tests and data collection. Prediction of aquifer response through time. Analog and computer analysis and interpretation of data.
GEOL 770.subject: GEOL
GEOL 770.title: Ground Water Geology

GEOL 771.description: Selected topics germane to the qualitative and quantitative aspects of the hydrologic cycle.
GEOL 771.subject: GEOL
GEOL 771.title: Topics in Hydrogeology

GEOL 772.description: Survey of the origin and development of geologic principles.
GEOL 772.subject: GEOL
GEOL 772.title: Geologic Theories

GEOL 773.description: The nature of water; physical, chemical, and biological quality parameters. Techniques of quantitative analysis, methods of water quality control, and pollution abatement. Hydrogeochemical interactions and effects on water quality and waste disposal.
GEOL 773.subject: GEOL
GEOL 773.title: Water Quality and Pollution

GEOL 774.description: Processes influencing conservative and reactive transport of solutes through porous media. Geochemistry of natural waters; transport processes for geologic and environmental/contaminant problems; mathematical equations; numerical methods; field techniques.
GEOL 774.subject: GEOL
GEOL 774.title: Solute Transport in Geologic Media

GEOL 775.description: Formation of groundwater flow and solute transport problems, theory and practice, numerical methods, solution techniques.
